title: Climbing Hangboard Load Progression
dataSources: Bar-velocity reps (`vbt:rep`), running gait (`gait:metric`), hangboard sessions (`hangboard:session`), golf-swing metrics (`golfswing:metric`), power-meter intervals (`powermeter:interval`), basketball shot arcs (`shotarc:make`).
app: Sports and skill sensors — velocity-based-training bar trackers, running-form IMUs, climbing hangboard load cells, golf launch monitors, cycling power meters, and computer-vision shot trackers — logged to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=hangboard:session
| timechart span=1w max(added_kg) as max_load, avg(hang_time_s) as avg_hang by grip
description: Trends the added weight and hang time you sustain on each grip type, charting finger-strength gains for climbing.
value: Finger strength is climbing's foundation and slow to build; trending hangboard load makes tiny weekly gains visible and motivating.
implementation: Ingest hangboard load-cell sessions into `index=personal`; review load and hang time by grip.
visualization: Multi-line chart of hangboard load by grip type.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how much weight your fingers can hold on the training board, showing your climbing strength grow.
